Description: There is a defined dense radiopacity in the right posterior mandible just superior to the inferior alveolar nerve canal and this is most consistent with a developmental entity dense bone island

There is a defind non corticated apical radiolucency associated with number 25 26 there are large coronal restorations on these teeth  along with widening of periodontal ligament space the apical radiolucency is continuous with widened periodontal ligament space with loss of lamina dura which is most consistent with inflammation the differential diagnosis for this would include apical rarefying osteitis
There is a defined dense radiopacity noted in the edentulous site number 19 this is consistent with developmental entity dense bone island

There is an apical radiolucency associated with a remnant root fragment number 29 there is a sclerotic band around this radiolucency this is consistent with inflammation apical rarefying and sclerosing osteitis

Number 1 there is widening of follicular spaces associated with impacted maxillary third molars- number 1 16 consistent with hyperplastic follicles developmental second area of interest defined dense radiopaque area between roots of tooth number 30 and 31 continuous with lamina of both the teeth no root resorption or displacement noted this is consistent with developmental dense bone island or idiopathic osteosclerosis

There is an apical radiolucency associated with tooth number 30 which is missing most of its coronal tooth structure there is also a sclerotic area around the apical radiolucencies with widening of periodontal ligament space this is consistent with inflammation apical rarefying and sclerosing osteitis
There is a defined dense radiopacity located between teeth number 28 and 29  that is continuous with a lamina dura of 29 this is consistent with developmental dense bone island

The right condyle looks larger in width compared to the left it is also shorter in height and the osseous trabecular pattern is atypical this is most consistent with trauma with displacement of the fracture fragment
There is a radiopaque area noted within the right maxillary sinus with well-defined borders.  This is most consistent with a benign entity such as an osteoma
There is an apical radiolucency associated with tooth number 19 with some sclerotic banding peripherally there may be slight distal root resorption this is most consistent with inflammation

There are defined radiopacities noted in the edentulous site corresponding to tooth number 32 these are consistent with remnant root fragments there is a periapical radiolucency associated with tooth number 10 most consistent with apical rarefying osteitis and inflammation
